method.label: Subtract a sector from the tangent quadrilateral

annotationRationale: Perpendicular tangent radii create special right triangles, whose lengths determine the quadrilateral area. Subtracting its 60-degree sector gives the curved gap.
sourceMethod: Follows the first official solution using the auxiliary intersection F, two special right triangles, and quadrilateral area minus sector area. Defines every auxiliary point in words and expands the quadrilateral area calculation.

review.mathCheck: The construction gives \(DF=24\), \(EF=12\), and \(AE=AG=4\sqrt3\), consistent with the supplied figure. Tangency lies on the triangle side. The quadrilateral area is \(48\sqrt3\), and its 60-degree sector has area \(24\pi\). The gap therefore yields \(48+3+24=75\), choice D.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, independently worded adaptation of MAA Q14's first approach on page 8. The point order, special-triangle lengths, tangent quadrilateral, and sector subtraction match the official figure and calculation.
review.annotationCheck: The text supplies enough construction detail to reconstruct the method without a separate diagram. Tangent properties and sector area are assessed; equilateral angles, special right triangles, and triangle area are suitable prerequisites.
